headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell overlap: Claude Code can write the repo while xonsh can execute and mutate the same workspace, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo/user files and can use MCP; xonsh reads/writes the filesystem and executes shell commands. That creates a default shared-file bridge where one agent can place attacker-controlled content that the other may treat as instructions. No clipboard bridge is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working directory or repo checkout
IF xonsh consumes files produced by Claude Code without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP for Claude Code unless needed
Require manual review of any file one agent asks the other to execute
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch filesystem contents, source code, configuration, and environment variables. Claude Code also handles git credentials and runs with no self-isolation, while xonsh has broad filesystem access. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive files into the other’s outputs; the pairwise leakage path is plausible in default terminal use.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or environment variables
IF either agent prints file contents or command output into logs or chat
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Unset secrets before launching either agent
Restrict shared directories to non-sensitive files
Turn off verbose logging and transcript capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state; xonsh can also execute shell and write the filesystem. Claude Code explicitly shares state via filesystem and git, so concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt work or commits. Because both can mutate the same mutable resources, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository or directory
IF either agent writes files while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use git worktrees or separate clones
Lock the repo before commits
Keep xonsh read-only during Claude Code runs
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, shell commands, and file edits that xonsh can immediately execute in the same terminal workflow. xonsh is a shell, so it may treat Claude Code output as authoritative unless the operator inserts verification. The pathway exists in default scripting workflows, but it is not inherently automatic.
conditions: IF xonsh executes commands or scripts copied from Claude Code output
IF no human verification step checks the generated commands before execution
mitigations: Require a second-person review for generated commands
Paste commands into a scratch buffer first
Use dry-run flags where available
Compare generated diffs before applying them
requires-engineering: add command allowlisting

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and runs on the host user, while xonsh is isolated and open-source with no requested secrets. The main compliance concern is local secret handling and retention in shared terminals, not a documented residency or certification mismatch. I cite only Claude Code because the specific compliance exposure is one-sided.
conditions: IF either agent is used on a machine containing regulated secrets
IF terminal history or logs retain credentials or sensitive command output
mitigations: Clear shell history after sensitive sessions
Avoid launching either agent in regulated environments
Rotate exposed credentials promptly
Use ephemeral shells for secret-bearing tasks
requires-engineering: implement retention controls
